title: Cube & Dice
summary: Dice questions ask for opposite faces from several positions (adjacent-four, two-common-faces and same-position rules), or from an unfolded net (skip one; ends of a Z). Painted-cube questions use 8, 12(n−2), 6(n−2)² and (n−2)³.

subtopics.title: Dice: finding opposite faces from positions
subtopics.concept: A die is a cube with six faces. Each face touches four faces and is opposite exactly one face. When several pictures of the same die are shown, use them to find which faces are opposite. Three quick rules do most of the work: strike out the neighbours, look for two common faces, and compare faces that sit in the same place.

formulas.name: Standard die
formulas.note: Opposite faces of a standard die add to 7.

formulas.name: Hidden faces of a standard die

tricks.title: Strike out the neighbours
tricks.body: List every face seen with the asked face and cross them out. If one face is left, it is the answer.

example.q: A face P is seen with Q and R, then with S and Q, then with R and T. Which face is opposite P?
steps: P was seen with Q, R, S and T.
These four all touch P.
Only U is left.

tricks.title: Two common faces
tricks.body: Two pictures with two faces in common: the two other faces are opposite.

example.q: One picture shows K, L, M. Another shows K, L, N. Which face is opposite M?
steps: K and L appear in both pictures.
The other faces, M and N, are opposite each other.

tricks.title: Hidden faces of a standard die
tricks.body: All six faces add to 21. Subtract the three faces you can see.

example.q: A standard die shows 2, 4 and 6. What do the three hidden faces add up to?
steps: Check: the hidden faces are 5, 3 and 1, and $5+3+1=9$.

mistakes.wrong: Saying two faces are opposite only because they never appear together.
mistakes.right: First strike out four neighbours, or use two common faces. Then the last face is opposite.

mistakes.wrong: Using the same-place rule when the common face is in a different place, or when a second face also repeats.
mistakes.right: Use it only for one common face in the same place. Otherwise use strike-out or two common faces.

mistakes.wrong: Using the sum 7 rule on a die that is not called standard.
mistakes.right: Check the question. Letters or unusual numbers have no sum rule.

mistakes.wrong: Choosing an option that shows two opposite faces together.
mistakes.right: Reject any picture that shows two faces from the same opposite pair.

mistakes.wrong: Mixing up left and right when rolling a die.
mistakes.right: Rolling right sends the top to the right side and brings the left face up. Say it aloud.

subtopics.notes:
### What one picture shows
A die has six faces. Each face touches four faces and is opposite one face.

A picture shows three faces that meet at one corner. These three faces all touch each other.

> **Rule:** Two faces seen together in one picture are never opposite.

### Strike out the neighbours
To find the face opposite X, list every face seen together with X. All of them touch X.

If four different faces are struck out, the one face left is opposite X.

Example: X is seen with A and B in one picture, with C in a second picture, and with D in a third. A, B, C and D all touch X. So the sixth face is opposite X.

> **Tip:** This rule needs no turning of the die. Try it first.

### Two common faces
Sometimes two pictures show the same two faces. Then the third face in each picture are opposite each other.

Pictures $(K, L, M)$ and $(K, L, N)$ share K and L. So M and N are opposite.

Why? The two faces that touch both K and L are exactly the two faces at the ends of the shared edge. They are opposite each other.

### One common face in the same place
Now two pictures share only one face X. X sits in the same place in both, for example on top. All other faces are different.

Then the faces in the same place are opposite: front with front, right with right.

Example: picture 1 has top A, front B, right C. Picture 2 has top A, front D, right E. So B is opposite D, C is opposite E, and F is opposite A.

> **Watch:** Use this rule only when the common face is in the same place and no other face repeats. If not, use the first two rules.

### Standard die
A standard (ordinary) die has opposite faces adding to 7: 1 and 6, 2 and 5, 3 and 4.

All six faces add to 21. So the hidden faces add to $21$ minus the three faces you can see.

> **Note:** Use the sum 7 rule only when the question says the die is standard. A die marked with letters has no sum rule.

### Rolling a die
Rolling a die moves its faces in a circle. The other two faces stay in place.

- Roll to the right: top goes to the right, right goes to the bottom, bottom goes to the left, left comes to the top.
- Roll forward: top goes to the front, front goes to the bottom, bottom goes to the back, back comes to the top.

Example: a standard die has 1 on top, 2 in front and 3 on the right. So 6 is at the bottom, 5 at the back and 4 on the left. Roll it once to the right: 4 comes to the top.

### Order of work
Write the three opposite pairs as you find them.

1. Look for two common faces. This gives a whole pair at once.
2. Look for a common face in the same place.
3. Strike out neighbours to finish the last pair.

patterns.name: Strike out the neighbours
patterns.howToSpot: Three pictures of one die. The asked face appears with four different faces across the pictures.
steps: List every face seen together with the asked face.
Strike them out. They all touch it.
The one face left is the answer.
patterns.why: Every face seen with X touches X, so the only face never seen with X must be opposite.

example.q: Three pictures of one cube show the faces (P, Q, R), (P, S, Q) and (P, R, T). Which face is opposite P?
steps: P is seen with Q, R, S and T.
These four faces all touch P.
Only U is left.

patterns.name: Two common faces
patterns.howToSpot: Two pictures repeat the same two faces. Each picture has one extra face.
steps: Find the two faces that appear in both pictures.
Note the extra face in each picture.
The two extra faces are opposite.
patterns.why: Only two faces touch both shared faces. They sit at the two ends of the shared edge.

example.q: One picture of a cube shows the faces K, L and M. Another picture shows K, L and N. Which face is opposite M?
steps: K and L are in both pictures.
The extra faces are M and N.
So M and N are opposite.

patterns.name: One common face in the same place
patterns.howToSpot: Two pictures share exactly one face. It sits in the same place in both, such as top in both.
steps: Check that the common face is in the same place.
Check that no other face repeats.
Pair the faces in matching places: front with front, right with right.
patterns.why: The four faces round the common face go in a circle, so faces in matching places end up across from each other.

example.q: In picture 1 a cube shows A on top, B in front and C on the right. In picture 2 it shows A on top, D in front and E on the right. Which face is opposite B?
steps: A is on top in both pictures.
No other face repeats.
Front faces are opposite: B and D.
(Right faces C and E are opposite. F is opposite A.)

patterns.name: Standard die (sum 7)
patterns.howToSpot: The question says ordinary or standard die and gives some face numbers.
steps: Pair the numbers: 1-6, 2-5, 3-4.
For a hidden face, take 7 minus its opposite.
For the hidden total, take 21 minus the shown faces.
patterns.why: Opposite faces add to 7, and all six faces add to 21.

example.q: A standard die shows 3 on top, 5 in front and 6 on the right. What is the sum of the three hidden faces?
steps: Check: the hidden faces are 4, 2 and 1.

patterns.name: Build the full opposite map
patterns.howToSpot: Three or more pictures. The question asks for one pair or for the partner of the last face.
steps: Use two common faces to find a pair.
Repeat with another two pictures.
The last two unpaired faces are opposite.
patterns.why: There are only three opposite pairs. Two known pairs leave the third.

example.q: Three pictures of a cube show (A, B, C), (A, B, D) and (B, C, E). Which face is opposite B?
steps: First and second pictures share A and B, so C is opposite D.
First and third pictures share B and C, so A is opposite E.
Only B and F are left, so B is opposite F.

patterns.name: Which picture is possible?
patterns.howToSpot: The opposite pairs are given in words. The options are pictures of three faces.
steps: Write the three opposite pairs.
Cross out any option that shows both faces of a pair.
The option with one face from each pair is possible.
patterns.why: A picture never shows two opposite faces. Three faces from three different pairs always meet at a corner.

example.q: On a cube, A is opposite D, B is opposite E and C is opposite F. Which set of three faces can be seen together? (1) A, D, C (2) B, E, F (3) A, B, F (4) C, F, B
steps: Option 1 has A and D. Option 2 has B and E.
Option 4 has C and F.
Option 3 has A, B and F, one from each pair.

patterns.name: Rolling the die
patterns.howToSpot: The die is rolled to the right, left, forward or back. The top, bottom or front face is asked.
steps: Write the six faces: top, bottom, front, back, left, right.
Roll right: left face comes to the top.
Roll forward: back face comes to the top.
Write the new positions after every roll.
patterns.why: A roll turns the die by a quarter turn, so four faces move in a circle and two stay.

example.q: A standard die shows 1 on top, 2 in front and 3 on the right. It is rolled once to the right and then once forward. Which number is now on top?
steps: Bottom 6, back 5, left 4 (each pair adds to 7).
Roll right: left face 4 comes to the top.
Now the back face is still 5.
Roll forward: the back face 5 comes to the top.

revision: A picture shows three faces at one corner. They all touch.
Strike out every face seen with X. Four struck out means the sixth is opposite.
Two common faces: the other two faces are opposite.
One common face in the same place: front with front, right with right.
Standard die: 1-6, 2-5, 3-4. Hidden faces add to 21 minus the shown faces.
Roll right: left face comes to the top. Roll forward: back face comes to the top.

subtopics.title: Cube nets: folding a sheet into a cube
subtopics.concept: A net is a flat sheet of six squares that folds into a cube. Squares that share an edge in the net touch on the cube. To find opposite faces, skip one square in a straight line, or take the two ends of a Z shape. To test a drawn cube, first reject any cube that shows two opposite faces.

tricks.title: Skip one
tricks.body: Along a row or column, skip one square. The squares on both sides of the skipped one are opposite.

example.q: A net has a row of four squares A, B, C, D. Which face is opposite B?
steps: Skip C.
B and D are opposite.

tricks.title: Reject first
tricks.body: In a which-cube question, throw out every option that shows an opposite pair. Often only one option is left.

example.q: In a net, A and C are opposite. Can a cube show A on top and C in front?
steps: A and C are opposite faces.
Opposite faces are never seen together.

mistakes.wrong: Calling two squares opposite because they are far apart in the net.
mistakes.right: Use the rules: skip one in a line, or the ends of a Z. Then use the three-pair check.

mistakes.wrong: Accepting a cube that shows two opposite faces.
mistakes.right: Find the opposite pairs first. Reject any option that shows both faces of a pair.

mistakes.wrong: Ignoring the order of the three faces round the corner.
mistakes.right: Check the counter-clockwise order. The mirror order can never be formed.

mistakes.wrong: Thinking the first and fourth squares of a row of four are opposite.
mistakes.right: Only the first and third, and the second and fourth, are opposite.

mistakes.wrong: Calling a shape with a 2 by 2 block or a row of five a net.
mistakes.right: Such shapes overlap when folded. They are not nets.

subtopics.notes:
### What a net is
A net is a flat sheet of six squares. Fold it and it becomes a cube. The printed side is on the outside.

Two squares that share an edge in the net touch on the cube. They are never opposite.

### Skip one in a straight line
In a straight row or column, two squares with exactly one square between them are opposite.

Row P, Q, R, S: P and R are opposite, and Q and S are opposite.

> **Rule:** Skip one square. First and third are opposite. Second and fourth are opposite.

The first and fourth squares of a row of four are not opposite. They touch when the row wraps round the cube.

### The Z shape
Find four squares in a Z or S shape: two squares, a step sideways, then two more. The two end squares are opposite.

Staircase net A, B, C, D, E, F: A, B, C, D form a Z, so A and D are opposite. B, C, D, E form a Z, so B and E are opposite. Then C and F are the last pair.

### Find all three pairs
A cube has three pairs of opposite faces. Find two pairs with the rules above. The two squares left over are the third pair.

Row A, B, C, D, with E above B and F below C: A-C and B-D come from the row. E and F are left, so they are opposite.

### Which shapes are nets
Only 11 shapes fold into a cube. Use two checks.

- No 2 by 2 block of squares.
- No row of five squares.

Six nets have a row of four, four nets have a row of three, and one is the staircase. Any shape with a 2 by 2 block or a row of five is not a net.

### Which cube can be formed
Each option shows three faces of a cube. Read them as top, front and right.

1. Find the opposite pairs in the net.
2. Reject any option that shows both faces of a pair.
3. For the rest, find the three squares in the net. Look for an L shape: one square touching the other two.
4. Read the three squares counter-clockwise round the point where they meet. The cube must show them counter-clockwise too: top, then front, then right.

> **Watch:** Two options can show the same three faces in different orders. Only one order is right. The other is the mirror image.

### Quick way to check a net
Fold the net in your head, one square at a time. Keep one square as the base.

- Fold the squares next to the base up as walls.
- Fold the last square over as the lid.
- If two squares land on the same face, the shape is not a net.

With practice, the row rule and the Z rule are faster than folding. Use folding only to double-check.

### Worked example
Net: row A, B, C, D with E above B and F below C. Opposite pairs: A-C, B-D, E-F.

Test a cube with top E, front A, right B. A, B, E form an L shape with B in the middle. Round their meeting point, counter-clockwise, the order is E, A, B. The cube shows top E, front A, right B, the same order. So it can be formed. Top E, front B, right A is its mirror image and cannot.

patterns.name: Opposite faces in a row
patterns.howToSpot: A net with a straight row or column of three or four squares. The face opposite a given face is asked.
steps: Find the straight line that holds the given square.
Skip one square along the line.
The square on the far side of the skipped one is opposite.
patterns.why: Folding the row round the cube brings the first and third squares to opposite sides.

example.q: A net is a row of four squares P, Q, R, S with T above Q and U below R. Which face is opposite Q?
steps: The row is P, Q, R, S.
Skip R. Q and S are opposite.

patterns.name: Ends of a Z shape
patterns.howToSpot: The net bends: two squares, a step sideways, two more squares.
steps: Find four squares that form a Z or S.
Mark the two end squares.
The end squares are opposite.
patterns.why: In a Z, the two end squares fold to opposite sides of the cube.

example.q: A net has six squares A, B, C, D, E, F in a staircase: A next to B, C above B, D right of C, E above D, F right of E. Which face is opposite A?
steps: A, B, C, D form a Z shape.
The ends of the Z are A and D.

patterns.name: Find all three pairs
patterns.howToSpot: The question asks for a pair of opposite faces, or the partner of the last face.
steps: Use the row rule to find two pairs.
Use the Z rule if a row rule does not give a pair.
The two squares left over are the last pair.
patterns.why: There are only three pairs, so two pairs fix the third.

example.q: A net has a row of four squares A, B, C, D. E is above B and F is below C. Which two faces are opposite?
steps: Row rule: A is opposite C, and B is opposite D.
E and F are left over.
So E and F are opposite.

patterns.name: Which cube can be formed?
patterns.howToSpot: A net is drawn. The options are cubes with three faces shown.
steps: Find the three pairs of opposite faces.
Reject any option that shows both faces of a pair.
For the rest, find the three squares in the net and read them counter-clockwise.
Pick the option that shows top, front, right in the same order.
patterns.why: A real cube never shows opposite faces together, and its corner keeps the order of the net.

example.q: A net is a row of four squares A, B, C, D with E above B and F below C. Which cube can be formed? Faces are given as (top, front, right). (1) E, A, B (2) E, B, A (3) A, C, B (4) E, F, B
steps: Opposite pairs: A-C, B-D, E-F.
Option 3 has A and C. Option 4 has E and F. Reject both.
Options 1 and 2 show A, B and E in opposite orders.
Round their meeting point in the net, counter-clockwise, the order is E, A, B. That is option 1.

patterns.name: Which cube cannot be formed?
patterns.howToSpot: The same setup, but the impossible cube is asked.
steps: Find the three pairs of opposite faces.
Check each option for an opposite pair.
If none shows a pair, check the counter-clockwise order.
The option with the wrong order is the answer.
patterns.why: Three options fold correctly. The odd one out has an opposite pair or a mirror-image order.

example.q: A net has a column of four squares K, M, O, J (K at the top). L is left of M and N is right of M. Faces are given as (top, front, right). Which cube cannot be formed? (1) K, L, M (2) K, M, N (3) M, L, O (4) M, O, L
steps: Opposite pairs: K-O, M-J, L-N. No option shows a pair.
Options 3 and 4 show the same faces M, L, O.
In the net, round their meeting point, counter-clockwise, the order is M, L, O.
Option 3 has that order. Option 4 is the mirror image.

patterns.name: Which shape is a net?
patterns.howToSpot: Several flat shapes of six squares are drawn. The one that folds into a cube is asked.
steps: Reject any shape with a 2 by 2 block.
Reject any shape with a row of five squares.
Fold the rest in your head or check the pairs.
patterns.why: Blocks and long rows put two squares on the same face, so the cube cannot close.

example.q: Which shape is a net of a cube? (a) five squares in a row, one below the middle square (b) a row of four squares, one above the second and one below the third (c) a 2 by 2 block with two more squares in a row on the right of the top one (d) two rows of three squares, the second row shifted one square to the right
steps: Shape (a) has a row of five.
Shapes (c) and (d) contain a 2 by 2 block.
Shape (b) has no block and no long row, and it folds into a cube.

revision: Squares that share an edge touch on the cube.
Row or column: skip one. First and third are opposite.
Z or S of four squares: the two ends are opposite.
Three pairs in all. The two leftover squares form the last pair.
Which cube: reject opposite pairs, then check the counter-clockwise order.
Not a net: a 2 by 2 block or a row of five squares.

subtopics.title: Painted cube cut into small cubes
subtopics.concept: A big cube of side n is painted on the outside and cut into n cubed small cubes. A small cube keeps paint only on the faces that were on the surface. Corners have 3 painted faces, edges have 2, face centres have 1, and the hidden core has none. Always use n minus 2 for edges, faces and the core.

formulas.name: Two faces painted
formulas.note: Cubes on the edges, not the corners.

formulas.name: One face painted
formulas.note: Cubes in the middle of each face.

formulas.name: Total check
formulas.note: The four counts add up to all the small cubes.

tricks.title: Check the total
tricks.body: The four counts must add up to n cubed. Use it to catch mistakes.

example.q: For a cube of side 5, check the four counts.
steps: Corners $8$; edges $12 \times 3 = 36$; faces $6 \times 9 = 54$; core $27$.

tricks.title: At least one painted
tricks.body: Take all the small cubes and remove the core.

example.q: A cube of side 6 is painted and cut. How many small cubes have at least one painted face?

mistakes.wrong: Using n instead of (n - 2) in the formulas.
mistakes.right: Edges, faces and the core all use (n - 2). Subtract 2 before you square or cube.

mistakes.wrong: Thinking the number of corner cubes changes with n.
mistakes.right: A cube always has 8 corners, so 3 painted faces always means 8 cubes.

mistakes.wrong: Counting corners again inside the edge cubes.
mistakes.right: Edge cubes are only the n - 2 cubes between the corners.

mistakes.wrong: Using the cube formulas for a cuboid.
mistakes.right: Use each side's own (side - 2): a - 2, b - 2 and c - 2.

mistakes.wrong: Forgetting to subtract the shared edge when only some faces are painted.
mistakes.right: Two painted faces that touch share one edge. Remove those cubes from the exactly-one count.

subtopics.notes:
### The idea
Take a big cube of side $n$. Paint all six faces. Cut it into $n \times n \times n$ small cubes.

A small cube keeps paint only on faces that were on the outside. Its position decides how many faces are painted.

### The four counts
| Painted faces | Where the cube is | How many |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | corner | $8$ |
| 2 | on an edge, not a corner | $12(n-2)$ |
| 1 | middle of a face | $6(n-2)^2$ |
| 0 | inside | $(n-2)^3$ |

For $n = 4$: $8$, $24$, $24$ and $8$. They add to $64$.

> **Rule:** Corners are always 8, whatever the size. Every other count uses $(n-2)$.

### Why n minus 2
Each edge has $n$ small cubes. Two of them are corners. That leaves $n-2$.

Each face has $n \times n$ small cubes. Remove the border ring and $(n-2) \times (n-2)$ are left.

Peel one layer off every side of the big cube. A core of $(n-2)^3$ cubes is left.

The four counts must add up to $n^3$. Try $n = 3$: $8 + 12 + 6 + 1 = 27$.

> **Tip:** If your counts do not add to $n^3$, one of them is wrong.

### At least questions
- At least one face painted: all cubes except the core, $n^3 - (n-2)^3$.
- At least two faces painted: corners plus edges, $8 + 12(n-2)$.

A cube of side 6 has $216 - 64 = 152$ cubes with at least one painted face.

### Finding n
Sometimes a count is given and $n$ is asked. Divide, then add 2.

If 24 cubes have exactly two painted faces, then $12(n-2) = 24$. So $n - 2 = 2$ and $n = 4$.

A big cube of side 12 cm is cut into small cubes of side 3 cm. Then $n = 12 \div 3 = 4$.

### Cuboids
For an $a \times b \times c$ block, each side keeps its own $(\text{side} - 2)$.

- Corners: $8$.
- Edges: $4[(a-2)+(b-2)+(c-2)]$.
- Faces: $2[(a-2)(b-2)+(b-2)(c-2)+(c-2)(a-2)]$.
- Core: $(a-2)(b-2)(c-2)$.

For $5 \times 4 \times 3$: edges $4(3+2+1) = 24$ and core $3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$.

### Worked example
A cube of side 5 is painted and cut into 125 small cubes.

1. Corners: $8$.
2. Edges: $12 \times 3 = 36$.
3. Face centres: $6 \times 3^2 = 54$.
4. Core: $3^3 = 27$.

Check: $8 + 36 + 54 + 27 = 125$. All counts are right.

### Only some faces painted
If only some faces are painted, count face by face. Each painted face has $n \times n$ small cubes. A cube on the edge shared by two painted faces is counted twice, so remove it.

Top and front painted, $n = 4$: $16 + 16 = 32$. The shared edge has 4 cubes with two painted faces. So exactly one painted face is $32 - 2 \times 4 = 24$.

> **Watch:** Two opposite painted faces share no cubes, so nothing is counted twice.

patterns.name: Three faces painted (corners)
patterns.howToSpot: A painted cube is cut up. The question asks for cubes with three painted faces.
steps: Recall that only corner cubes have three painted faces.
A cube has 8 corners.
patterns.why: A small cube touches three big faces only at a corner of the big cube.

example.q: A cube of side 7 is painted on all faces and cut into small cubes of side 1. How many small cubes have three painted faces?
steps: Only the corner cubes have three painted faces.
A cube has 8 corners.

patterns.name: Two faces painted (edges)
patterns.howToSpot: The question asks for cubes with exactly two painted faces.
steps: Find n, the number of small cubes along one edge.
Each edge has n - 2 cubes that are not corners.
Multiply by 12 edges.
patterns.why: Each of the 12 edges has n cubes, and 2 of them are corners.

example.q: A cube of side 5 is painted and cut into 125 small cubes. How many have exactly two painted faces?
steps: $n = 5$, so each edge has $5 - 2 = 3$ such cubes.

patterns.name: One face painted (face centres)
patterns.howToSpot: The question asks for cubes with exactly one painted face.
steps: Find n.
On each face, remove the border ring. A block of (n - 2) by (n - 2) is left.
Multiply by 6 faces.
patterns.why: Cubes in the middle of a face touch no edge, so they have only that one face painted.

example.q: A cube of side 6 is painted and cut into small cubes of side 1. How many have exactly one painted face?
steps: One face: $4 \times 4 = 16$.

patterns.name: No face painted (core)
patterns.howToSpot: The question asks for cubes with no paint at all.
steps: Find n.
Peel one layer off every side.
Cube the side that is left: (n - 2) cubed.
patterns.why: The cubes inside never touched the outside, so they stay unpainted.

example.q: A cube of side 5 is painted and cut into small cubes of side 1. How many small cubes have no painted face?

patterns.name: At least or combined counts
patterns.howToSpot: The question says at least one, at least two, or asks for two classes added together.
steps: At least one painted: all cubes minus the core.
At least two painted: corners plus edges.
For any other mix, add the classes you need.
patterns.why: Every class is already counted, so a combined count is a sum of classes.

example.q: A cube of side 4 is painted and cut into small cubes of side 1. How many have at least two painted faces?
steps: Corners: $8$.
Edges: $12 \times 2 = 24$.

patterns.name: Painted cuboid
patterns.howToSpot: The block is a by b by c, not a cube.
steps: Write a - 2, b - 2 and c - 2.
Corners: 8.
Edges: 4 times the sum of the three (side - 2) values.
Faces and core use products of the (side - 2) values.
patterns.why: Each side of a cuboid has its own length, so each keeps its own (side - 2).

example.q: A cuboid measuring 5 by 4 by 3 is painted and cut into small cubes of side 1. How many have exactly two painted faces?

patterns.name: Find n from a count or a size
patterns.howToSpot: A count of painted cubes, or the edge lengths of the big and small cubes, is given. Another count is asked.
steps: Turn the given count into n: divide by 12 (edges) or by 6 and take the square root (faces).
Add 2 to get n. If edges are in cm, n = big edge divided by small edge.
Now find the count that is asked.
patterns.why: The formulas run both ways, so a count fixes n.

example.q: 36 small cubes have exactly two painted faces. How many small cubes have exactly one painted face?
steps: One face: $6 \times 3^2 = 54$.

patterns.name: Only some faces painted
patterns.howToSpot: The question says which faces are painted, such as the top and one side, or two opposite faces.
steps: Count the small cubes on each painted face: n times n.
If two painted faces touch, they share an edge of n cubes.
Exactly one painted face = sum of faces minus twice the shared cubes.
patterns.why: The cubes on a shared edge have two painted faces, so they must leave the exactly-one count.

example.q: A cube of side 4 is painted on its top face and on its front face only. It is cut into 64 small cubes. How many have exactly one painted face?
steps: Top face: $4 \times 4 = 16$. Front face: $16$.
The shared edge has 4 cubes with two painted faces.

revision: 3 painted faces: 8 corners, for any n.
At least one: $n^3 - (n-2)^3$. At least two: $8 + 12(n-2)$.
Given a count? Divide, then add 2 to get n.

The cube with K and O together and the one with J and M together are impossible. solvedExamples.q: A cube of side 4 cm is painted red on all its faces and then cut into small cubes of side 1 cm. How many small cubes have **exactly two** faces painted?
solvedExamples.solution: n = 4. Cubes with exactly two painted faces lie along the 12 edges, excluding the corners: each edge has n − 2 = 2 of them. Total 12 × 2 = **24**.

practice.q: An ordinary die, whose opposite faces always add up to 7, shows 2 on top, 6 in front and 4 on the right. What is the sum of the numbers on the bottom, back and left faces?
practice.solution: Opposite faces add to 7: bottom = 7 − 2 = 5, back = 7 − 6 = 1, left = 7 − 4 = 3. Sum = 5 + 1 + 3 = **9**.

With D facing you and B folded over the top, C (to the right of B in the net) comes down on the right side and A on the left. So B top, D front, C right is correct; B top, D front, A right is its mirror and cannot be formed.
practice.shortcut: Opposite pairs out; then fold around the front face.

practice.q: A cube of side 5 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have **exactly one** face painted?
practice.solution: Each face has a (5 − 2) × (5 − 2) = 9 block of cubes with only that face painted. 6 faces × 9 = **54**.

practice.q: A cube of side 6 units is painted on all faces and then cut into 216 unit cubes. How many unit cubes have **no** face painted?
practice.solution: Remove the outer layer on every side: the unpainted core is (6 − 2)³ = 4³ = **64**.

practice.q: A cuboid 5 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have **exactly two** faces painted?
practice.solution: Two-face cubes lie on the edges, excluding corners. There are 4 edges of each length: 4 × (5 − 2) + 4 × (4 − 2) + 4 × (3 − 2) = 12 + 8 + 4 = **24**.

practice.q: An ordinary die, whose opposite faces always add up to 7, shows **3** on top, **5** in front and **6** on the right. What is the sum of the numbers on the bottom, back and left faces?
practice.solution: Opposite faces add to 7: bottom = 7 − 3 = 4, back = 7 − 5 = 2, left = 7 − 6 = 1. Sum = 4 + 2 + 1 = **7**. (Check: 3 × 7 − 14 = 7.)
practice.shortcut: Hidden sum = 21 − (shown sum).

practice.q: An ordinary die, whose opposite faces always add up to 7, shows **2** on its top face. Which of the numbers 1 to 6 can **never** lie on a face adjacent to the 2?
practice.solution: The face opposite 2 is 7 − 2 = **5**. Opposite faces never touch, so 5 can never be adjacent to 2; every other number (1, 3, 4, 6) shares an edge with the 2 in some position.

practice.solution: The opposite pairs are K–M, L–N, O–P. Three of the options only use faces that fold next to each other in an order the cube allows; the remaining option cannot be turned to match — it either shows an opposite pair or runs the faces the wrong way round the corner. That one cannot be formed.
practice.shortcut: Three cubes fold; find the one with a pair or a mirrored corner.

practice.q: A cube of side 6 cm is painted on all its faces and then cut into small cubes of side 1 cm. How many small cubes have **three** faces painted?
practice.solution: Only the corner cubes of the big cube touch three painted faces, and a cube has 8 corners whatever its side. Answer **8**.

practice.q: A cube of side 7 units is painted on all faces and cut into 343 unit cubes. How many unit cubes have **exactly three** painted faces?
practice.solution: Three painted faces happen only at the corners of the big cube: **8** of them, independent of the side length.

practice.q: A cube of side 5 cm is painted on all its faces and then cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have **exactly two** faces painted?
practice.solution: Exactly-two cubes sit on the 12 edges, excluding the 2 corner cubes of each edge: 12 × (5 − 2) = 12 × 3 = **36**.

practice.q: A painted cube of side 6 is cut into unit cubes. How many unit cubes have exactly two painted faces?
practice.solution: Each of the 12 edges keeps 6 − 2 = 4 non-corner cubes: 12 × 4 = **48**.

practice.q: A cube of side 4 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have **exactly one** face painted?
practice.solution: On each face the cubes away from the edge form a (4 − 2) × (4 − 2) = 2 × 2 block. 6 faces × 4 = **24**.

practice.q: A painted cube of side 6 is cut into unit cubes. How many unit cubes have exactly one painted face?
practice.solution: Each face keeps an (6 − 2)² = 16 block of one-face cubes: 6 × 16 = **96**.

practice.q: A cube of side 5 cm is painted on all its faces and then cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have **no** face painted?
practice.solution: Strip one layer from every side: the unpainted core is (5 − 2)³ = 3³ = **27**.

practice.q: A painted cube of side 6 is cut into 216 unit cubes. How many unit cubes have no painted face?
practice.solution: The inner block measures (6 − 2) × (6 − 2) × (6 − 2) = 4³ = **64**.

practice.q: A cube of side 4 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have **at least two** painted faces?
practice.solution: Corners plus edge cubes: 8 + 12 × (4 − 2) = 8 + 24 = **32**.
practice.shortcut: At least two = corners + edges = 8 + 12(n − 2).

practice.q: A painted cube of side 5 is cut into unit cubes. How many unit cubes have paint on **at least one** face?
practice.solution: Everything except the hidden core: 5³ − (5 − 2)³ = 125 − 27 = **98**.
practice.shortcut: At least one = n³ − (n − 2)³.

practice.q: A cuboid 6 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have **no** face painted?
practice.solution: Strip one layer from each side: the core measures (6 − 2) × (4 − 2) × (3 − 2) = 4 × 2 × 1 = **8**.

practice.q: A cuboid 6 × 5 × 4 is painted on all faces and cut into unit cubes. How many unit cubes have **exactly one** face painted?
practice.solution: Each pair of opposite faces keeps a block away from the edges: 2 × [(6 − 2)(5 − 2) + (5 − 2)(4 − 2) + (4 − 2)(6 − 2)] = 2 × (12 + 6 + 8) = 2 × 26 = **52**.

practice.q: A cube is painted on all its faces and cut into identical small cubes. Exactly **36** small cubes have exactly two painted faces. How many small cubes have exactly **one** painted face?
practice.solution: 12(n − 2) = 36 gives n − 2 = 3, so n = 5. Then one-face cubes = 6(n − 2)² = 6 × 3² = 6 × 0 = **54**.
practice.shortcut: Divide by 12 to get n − 2, then use 6(n − 2)².

practice.q: A painted cube is cut into unit cubes, and exactly **48** of them have exactly two painted faces. How many unit cubes have **no** painted face?
practice.solution: 12(n − 2) = 48 gives n − 2 = 4, so n = 6. The unpainted core is (n − 2)³ = 4³ = **64**.
practice.shortcut: Find n from 12(n − 2), then use (n − 2)³.
